name:
Example: 
                    Computing a Limit at a Vertical Asymptote of Tangent
worked_solution:
First, let's try direct substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-\pi /6)^{-}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3}) & ={lim}_{x\to (-\pi /6)^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{3})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{-1}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

which is not defined.

Therefore, to find the limit, let's sketch the graph of $y =   \tan\left(x-\dfrac\pi 3 \right).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14258704/assets/e201daa486919eaba9f209334ef904a18415f14563da5c85e63047a2d149f3b3.png)

We see that as $x$ approaches $-\dfrac\pi 6$ from the left, the values of $y=\tan\left(x-\dfrac\pi 3 \right)$ are positive and increase without bound. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\lim_\limits {x \to (-\pi/6)^{-}} \tan\left(x-\dfrac\pi 3 \right)= \infty.
$$
